Definition: from G2095 and G1380; to think well of, i.e. approve (an act); specially, to approbate (a person or thing):--think good, (be well) please(-d), be the good (have, take) pleasure, be willing.
BiblicalUsage: eudokéō is a plain word for think good, (be well) please(-d), be the good (have, take) pleasure, be willing. In Matthew 3:17, the text says "in whom I am well pleased." In Mark 1:11, the text says "in whom I am well pleased."
TheologicalSignificance: eudokéō convinces me that grace is God giving what we could never earn, and never taking it back. That is why I keep this word in mind when I read those passages — it carries more than its size suggests.
RelatedTopics: God's Will; Grace; Love of God
